domain_description: Geospatial analysis for oil and gas land management covering land survey interpretation, GIS mapping and spatial analysis, plat reading and analysis, boundary dispute resolution, and mineral estate mapping. Integrates legal survey descriptions with modern GIS technology for accurate spatial representation of property rights, well locations, and infrastructure corridors. Grounded in PLSS standards, ALTA/NSPS survey standards, Texas Natural Resources Code, and state surveying regulations.
authority_sources: Public Land Survey System (PLSS) Manual of Instructions (BLM 2009)
Texas Administrative Code Title 22, Part 29 (Board of Professional Land Surveying)
National Standard for Spatial Data Accuracy (NSSDA)
Texas Society of Professional Surveyors Standards of Practice
Railroad Commission of Texas GIS and Mapping Standards

engines.name: Land Survey Analysis Engine
engines.function: Interpret and analyze land survey descriptions including metes and bounds, PLSS aliquot part descriptions, lot and block references, and survey plats. Validate legal descriptions, identify ambiguities, and calculate acreage from survey data.
doctrine_topics: metes and bounds description interpretation
PLSS aliquot part and section descriptions
Texas Abstract and survey system
lot and block subdivision descriptions
legal description ambiguity resolution rules
calls and monuments priority hierarchy
course and distance calculation and verification
acreage calculation from legal descriptions
survey overlap and gap identification
senior vs junior survey priority doctrine

golden_queries.question: A deed describes property as 'the NE/4 of Section 12, Block C-23, PSL Survey, Reeves County, Texas, SAVE AND EXCEPT the East 20 acres thereof.' Calculate the excepted tract dimensions and remaining acreage, and identify any ambiguity in the exception language.
required_elements: NE/4 section acreage calculation (160 acres)
East 20 acres tract dimension calculation
ambiguity in 'East 20 acres' (shape not specified)
survey monument and boundary identification
remaining acreage after exception

golden_queries.question: A metes and bounds description in a 1938 deed calls for 'North 45 degrees East, 1320 varas to a rock mound on the East bank of Pecos River.' The river has shifted 200 feet west since 1938. What controls — the bearing and distance or the natural monument?
required_elements: monument over distance priority rule
natural monument (river) vs artificial monument (rock mound)
ambulatory boundary doctrine for rivers
avulsion vs accretion analysis
vara to feet conversion (1 vara = 33.33 inches)

engines.name: GIS Mapping Engine
engines.function: Create and analyze Geographic Information System datasets for oil and gas land management including spatial data integration, coordinate transformation, thematic mapping, and spatial analysis of mineral ownership, well locations, and infrastructure.
doctrine_topics: coordinate reference systems (NAD83, WGS84, State Plane)
datum transformation and projection selection
spatial data layer creation and management
attribute table design for mineral ownership
topology rules for land parcel data
geocoding and address matching for well locations
spatial join and overlay analysis techniques
raster and vector data integration
web mapping service (WMS/WFS) integration
GIS data quality assurance and accuracy standards

golden_queries.question: Design a GIS database schema for tracking mineral ownership across a 50-section study area in the Permian Basin. The database must support fractional mineral interests, multiple lessees per tract, well locations, pipeline corridors, and unit boundaries. Specify the coordinate system, layer structure, and attribute tables.
required_elements: Texas State Plane coordinate system selection
mineral ownership polygon layer with fractional interest attributes
well point layer with RRC API number linkage
pipeline corridor linear features with easement width
temporal versioning for ownership changes
failure_signals: no relational database design for interests

engines.name: Plat Analysis Engine
engines.function: Read, interpret, and analyze survey plats, subdivision plats, and unit plats for oil and gas operations. Extract legal descriptions, verify dimensions, identify easements and restrictions, and cross-reference with deed records.
doctrine_topics: survey plat reading and interpretation
subdivision plat analysis and lot identification
RRC unit plat requirements and format
plat scale and dimension verification
easement and right-of-way identification on plats
plat filing and recording requirements
replat and plat amendment procedures
plat to deed description reconciliation
pipeline and utility location on plats
digital plat creation and CAD integration

golden_queries.question: An RRC spacing unit plat shows a 640-acre unit comprising 4 quarter sections from 2 different surveys. The plat indicates the proposed well location is 467 feet from the north line and 660 feet from the east line of the SE/4 of Section 5. Verify the well location meets Rule 37 spacing requirements and identify any potential issues with the multi-survey unit.
required_elements: Rule 37 minimum distance requirements (467/1200)
multi-survey unit boundary verification
well location coordinate calculation
survey gap or overlap analysis at survey boundaries
setback compliance from all lease lines
failure_signals: failure to address multi-survey boundary issues

engines.name: Boundary Dispute Engine
engines.function: Analyze real property boundary disputes including survey conflicts, adverse possession claims, boundary by acquiescence, and the resolution of overlapping property descriptions using legal principles and surveying evidence.
doctrine_topics: boundary dispute resolution principles
adverse possession elements and proof (Texas 10-year statute)
boundary by acquiescence doctrine
agreed boundary doctrine
survey conflict resolution (senior vs junior surveys)
expert surveyor testimony and evidence standards
quiet title action for boundary disputes
fence line vs legal boundary analysis
riparian boundary ambulatory principles
mineral boundary disputes (horizontal vs vertical severance)

golden_queries.question: Two adjacent ranch owners have maintained a fence line for 40 years that a new survey reveals is 150 feet east of the actual property boundary, enclosing 12 acres of the eastern neighbor's land. The western neighbor has improved, grazed, and paid taxes on the disputed strip. Minerals have been severed and the western neighbor's lessee has a producing well in the disputed strip. Analyze the boundary dispute including both surface and mineral rights.
required_elements: adverse possession elements under Texas law
boundary by acquiescence analysis
mineral rights treatment in adverse possession
color of title vs limitations title analysis
impact on existing oil and gas lease and production
failure_signals: failure to address mineral rights separately
no discussion of producing well impact

engines.name: Mineral Estate Mapping Engine
engines.function: Map and visualize mineral estate ownership patterns including severed mineral interests, fractional ownership, leasehold positions, and the spatial relationship between mineral estates, well locations, spacing units, and geological formations.
doctrine_topics: mineral estate ownership polygon creation
fractional mineral interest spatial representation
vertical mineral estate mapping (depth severance)
horizontal well lateral path and formation mapping
spacing unit and pooled unit spatial analysis
lease expiration and HBP area mapping
geological formation mapping and cross-section
mineral ownership change tracking over time
net mineral acre calculation and mapping
unleased mineral acreage identification

golden_queries.question: Create a mineral estate map for Section 15 where the minerals have been severed 6 times since 1940, with depth severances at 5,000 feet and 10,000 feet, 3 existing horizontal wells (2 in the Wolfcamp A, 1 in the Bone Spring), and 2 pooled units that overlap the section boundaries. Describe the mapping methodology and layers required.
required_elements: temporal ownership chain mapping methodology
depth severance visualization (3D or stacked 2D)
horizontal well lateral path mapping with formation
pooled unit boundary overlay with section
net mineral acre calculation per depth zone
failure_signals: failure to integrate well data with ownership
